$comment: Known divergences from the canonical implementation (HMD-0020 §10). Each entry names something this implementation is expected to get wrong, and why: `cases` are conformance cases, `rules` are lint rules it does not emit at all, `rendering` is HTML that differs. An entry that stops diverging fails the build — a ledgered case that PASSES, or a ledgered rule this implementation actually emits — because an expected failure that starts succeeding and is not removed is how a ledger rots into a lie.

rules.reason: The publication model behind it is unported. `nav` is a mapping of `order` and `visibility` in the canonical implementation, visibility inherits from the nearest ancestor folder note and defaults to private, and HMD017 warns when a published card links to a card that is not. This implementation still reads the HMD-0001 closed key set of `tags`, `use`, `import`, ignores `nav` entirely, and has no notion of a card being published — so it emits no HMD017 anywhere. Parity therefore drops HMD017 from the canonical side before comparing; every other rule is still compared byte for byte.

rendering.reason: Raw HTML in a card is escaped rather than passed through. Deliberate: a webview rendering workspace HTML is a script-injection surface reachable from any cloned repository.
`~x~` subscript is unsupported; markdown-it's builtin only covers `~~strikethrough~~`.

markdown-it recognises setext headings (`Title` over `=====`); the canonical scanner finds ATX headings only, so a setext heading has no slug on the Python side and is not addressable by `[[Page#Section]]`.
Column numbers count UTF-16 code units here and code points in Python, so a diagnostic after an emoji on the same line can differ by one per astral character.
Math is typeset by KaTeX here and by whatever MathJax the MkDocs site loads there. Both render the same LaTeX; the HTML around it differs.
